info.title: openrouter/images
info.description: The request body Comfy Router accepts for the model "openrouter/images", and the response body it returns. The INPUT schema is the same schema the server validates a call against before it reaches the provider, so what is published and what is enforced cannot differ. `x-comfy-router-input-modalities` records the media kinds the model is documented to accept; the request schema is shared across sibling models and may admit media kinds this model ignores. The OUTPUT schema describes the provider's native result document exactly as Router returns it: Router does not validate, narrow or re-envelope the response, so the output schema is descriptive rather than enforced, and Comfy owns no output shape of its own.

schema.description:
Image generation request.

`model` is CALLER-CHOSEN and is not resolved by Comfy Router: the Router model ID `openrouter/images` names this operation, not a model, and the `model` you send is forwarded to OpenRouter unchanged. Use OpenRouter's own model IDs, such as `microsoft/mai-image-2.6`, which carry a `/` that a `{provider}/{model}` Router ID cannot spell. A request with no `model` is rejected with a 400.

input_references.description: Reference images for image-to-image generation, as data URLs or HTTP(S) URLs

model.description: The image generation model to use, as an OpenRouter model ID such as `microsoft/mai-image-2.6` or `microsoft/mai-image-2.6-flash`.

prompt.description: Text description of the desired image

stream.description: Enable SSE streaming for partial images. The `/proxy/` route rejects `stream: true` with a 400. Comfy Router sets it to false and serves the request.

b64_json.description: Base64-encoded image data. When the response is larger than 1,048,576 bytes, Comfy Router answers `url` in its place. The image stays here when the response is not larger than that, or when its upload to Comfy storage fails.

url.description: A Comfy-hosted signed URL of the image, given in place of `b64_json` when the response is larger than 1,048,576 bytes. Comfy Router always asks for it; the `/proxy/` route asks for it only when the request sends `Comfy-Asset-Format: url`. A zero-data-retention workspace never gets it: its images stay in `b64_json`. The URL expires 24 hours after the call.

OpenRouterPreferredMaxLatency.description: Preferred maximum latency (in seconds). Can be a number (applies to p50) or an object with percentile-specific cutoffs. Endpoints above the threshold(s) may still be used, but are deprioritized in routing. When using fallback models, this may cause a fallback model to be used instead of the primary model if it meets the threshold.

Endpoints below the threshold(s) may still be used, but are deprioritized in routing. When using fallback models, this may cause a fallback model to be used instead of the primary model if it meets the threshold.

OpenRouterProviderPreferences.description: When multiple model providers are available, optionally indicate your routing preference.

allow_fallbacks.description:
Whether to allow backup providers to serve requests
- true: (default) when the primary provider (or your custom providers in "order") is unavailable, use the next best provider.
- false: use only the primary/custom provider, and return the upstream error if it's unavailable.

data_collection.description:
Data collection setting. If no available model provider meets the requirement, your request will return an error.
- allow: (default) allow providers which store user data non-transiently and may train on it

- deny: use only providers which do not collect user data.

enforce_distillable_text.description: Whether to restrict routing to only models that allow text distillation. When true, only models where the author has allowed distillation will be used.

ignore.description: List of provider slugs to ignore. If provided, this list is merged with your account-wide ignored provider settings for this request.

only.description: List of provider slugs to allow. If provided, this list is merged with your account-wide allowed provider settings for this request.

order.description: An ordered list of provider slugs. The router will attempt to use the first provider in the subset of this list that supports your requested model, and fall back to the next if it is unavailable. If no providers are available, the request will fail with an error message.

quantizations.description: A list of quantization levels to filter the provider by.

require_parameters.description: Whether to filter providers to only those that support the parameters you've provided. If this setting is omitted or set to false, then providers will receive only the parameters they support, and ignore the rest.

zdr.description: Whether to restrict routing to only ZDR (Zero Data Retention) endpoints. When true, only endpoints that do not retain prompts will be used.
